naming_clarity.reason: Everyday stakeholder language (driver, cold morning, towing a trailer up a mountain pass, charging speed I was promised, warranty, uneven ageing); rated to deliver continuously is a standard rating phrase a non-implementer can follow.

no_mechanism_leak.reason: Describes behaviour only (the pack warming and cooling itself, drive power falling off, a reduced fallback power, a workshop warning) and names no class, function, module, table, endpoint, signal or technology.

parent_fit.reason: Root of the V: the user_stories stage has no upstream stage (depends_on is empty) and the story has no outgoing trace link, so there is no parent to engage with and the axis is fully met by default.

single_user_capability.reason: Bundles at least three independently deliverable capabilities under thermal management: heating and cooling calls, thermal power limiting (gradual fall-off near the limit, reduced power when the heating and cooling system stops responding, and the sustained-load current cap of the towing case), and a workshop warning for a wide cell-temperature spread; each could ship without the others and the warning has a different observer.
single_user_capability.suggestion: Split into a thermal-conditioning story (heating and cooling), a thermal power-limiting story (derating and the fallback) and a thermal-imbalance warning story; the towing / continuous-current clause is a distinct current-limit promise that no requirement in the graph states (REQ_PACK_OVERCURRENT is a 350 A / 100 ms contactor trip, not a continuous-rating cap), so give it its own story and requirement or remove it.

user_observable.reason: Partly directly observable (power falls off gradually, a reduced-power fallback, a workshop warning), but much of the paragraph is framed through the requests and limits of the pack itself (calls for heating, calls for cooling, never draws more current than its cells are rated) with no observer or visible effect named, so the user-visible effect is harder to see than it should be.
user_observable.suggestion: Describe heating and cooling by what is seen (the pack warms or cools and the promised charging speed holds, or the workshop reads the request) and say how the sustained-load limit is observed, e.g. a road or bench test measuring pack current against the cell rating.

summary: Plain and implementation-free, but it bundles heating/cooling, thermal power limiting (including an unbacked sustained-load current cap) and a workshop spread warning, and part of its observable paragraph is interface-level.
